companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The health insurance company that serves tens of millions of customers in the U.S. reported fiscal year 2022 revenue of $92.9 billion, up 10% from the previous year, thanks in part to growth in membership and premiums from its Medicare Advantage plans.

  • Humana announced plans in February 2022 to reinvest $1 billion into its core business, specifically its Medicare Advantage plan.

  • In May 2022, Humana’s CenterWell Senior Primary Care and the investment firm Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe announced a joint venture to develop and operate primary care clinics for Medicare patients, the second such JV between the two partners.

  • In 2023, Humana anticipates strong growth from its privately run Medicare Advantage program due to high retention and a projected expansion in new members.

  • Humana has climbed 10 spots on the Fortune 500 list in the last four years.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Founded in 1961, Humana is the fifth-largest health insurance company by membership in the U.S., offering coverage for over 20 million Americans. The company’s revenue grew to $83.1 billion in 2021, a 7.7% increase in revenue from 2020. Much of that growth was driven by Humana’s Medicare Advantage programs, which enroll roughly 5 million people; the company projects that membership in those programs will grow by another 8% in 2022. In April 2022, Humana announced the sale of a 60% stake in KAH Hospice, the nation’s largest home health and hospice provider, for $2.8 billion to private investment firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Health insurers have been looking like pretty good bets in the short term. A lot of that has to do with a suspension of health insurance industry fees, designed to reduce the industry’s tax burden, which was implemented in 2019. But Humana owes much of its own recent success to its focus on lucrative for-profit markets like Medicare Advantage, where the company expects membership to swell by more than 10% over the coming year. In May 2021, Humana plotted its next big evolutionary move by obtaining full ownership of home health care services firm Kindred at Home—a leader in a space that’s likely to see continued growth, given the steady aging of the overall population and the normalization of nonhospital care during the pandemic.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: In 2019, the health insurer's consolidated revenues grew to nearly $56.5 billion, a more than $8 billion spike from the previous year. Like other insurers, Humana was able to take advantage of the suspension of a health insurance industry fee, which lowered its tax burden. The company also boosted its earnings-per-share numbers with the help of stock buybacks. Humana’s dedication to the lucrative Medicare Advantage market, where it has captured some 18% of enrollment, continues to serve it well.

Humana’s dedication to the ever-lucrative Medicare market, as a for-profit insurer, continues to serve it well.

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
